chapter: Radio color line, San Francisco and Columbia staff
title: The Downbeat Club on Central Avenue and Mingus on bass
summary: Back in Los Angeles Lee led bands at the Downbeat Club, with Charles Mingus on bass, down the street from Johnny Otis.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: I did then, but I wouldn't now. But anyway, we came back down and I think, I kind of reorganized, and I went to the Downbeat Club on Central Avenue, right? In that band ... let's see now, was this the time I had Lucky?
I had a couple of bands at the Downbeat, and I don't know which came first. At one time, I had Marshall Royal, and yeah ... that came later; this is about right.

At the Downbeat, I had Russell Jack, Eleanor's brother, was playing trumpet; marvelous pianist -- what was that guy's name? I can see him, but ... really good pianist, and Charlie Mingus was playing bass with me. At the Downbeat. What happened is Johnny Otis was at the Club Alabam, which was 3 doors down, so Stan Kenton -- and I have it in right order -- Stan Kenton came on the Avenue because he was looking for a drummer, and someone told him to come hear Johnny Otis. Okay.
